1_score_arithmetic_97_100_vs_SKILL_345.verdict: VERIFIED — the contradiction is real, and it is narrow.
1_score_arithmetic_97_100_vs_SKILL_345.the_instruction: references/score-arithmetic.md:97-100 — 'State the denominator beside the score, so the reader can apply §3 without reconstructing it: `A Score: 75/100 — 15 points over 2 scored items; A01–A04, A06, A08–A10 N/A (requires site-level data)`. Scored + N/A = 10 in every dimension and 80 across the report, and the N/A list in the prose has to match the N/A rows in the tables.'
1_score_arithmetic_97_100_vs_SKILL_345.the_rule_it_contradicts: SKILL.md:345 — '**no framework item ID appears in the client-facing prose** … **A bare list of IDs inside a cell does not qualify either**: "C02, C03 Pass; C01 Partial" is the referent form wearing a table's clothes, because no plain-language name sits against any of them.'
1_score_arithmetic_97_100_vs_SKILL_345.why_it_contradicts_under_the_2026_08_17_: The ruling permits an ID as a ROW LABEL in a scored table, with the item's plain-language name beside it in the same row, and as the `**[ID] [Name]** — [suggestion]` heading of a Top-5 entry. `A01–A04, A06, A08–A10 N/A (requires site-level data)` is neither: it is a bare enumeration of eight IDs with no plain-language name against any of them, and it sits in a prose line the file tells the auditor to print 'beside the score' for 'the reader' — the reader of the report, i.e. the client. It is precisely the banned form. §7 item 2 compounds it by requiring 'the prose N/A list matches the N/A rows in the tables', which presumes such a list exists.
1_score_arithmetic_97_100_vs_SKILL_345.reach: One instruction and its checklist echo, in one file. references/item-reference.md carries no equivalent; SKILL.md carries none; the shared framework files carry none.
1_score_arithmetic_97_100_vs_SKILL_345.effect_on_this_run: None on any verdict. The deliverables resolved it in favour of SKILL.md:345: a scripted scan for framework item IDs outside scored-table row labels and outside fenced operator blocks returns ZERO hits in all five deliverables. Where the reference would have had them print an ID list, they wrote plain language — e1.md:232-234 'All ten items unevaluable, so this dimension carries no score and is excluded from the weighted total', e3.md:112-115 'Ten of them are the whole Authority dimension and seven are Trust items; the other two are the structured-data and semantic-markup items'.
1_score_arithmetic_97_100_vs_SKILL_345.note_for_the_fixer: The reference's underlying requirement — state the denominator so a reader can run §3 — is sound and is met by the deliverables ('87.5/100 … 35 points over 4 scored items'). Only the ID list in the worked string is out. The narrowest fix is to replace the ID enumeration in the example with the count plus a plain-language reason, since the tables already carry the per-item detail the ruling protects.

2_potential_gain_shortcut.verdict: The record's claim that content-quality-auditor 'runs the same rescale but states no shortcut' is REFUTED. It states a shortcut, in two places, and the shortcut is CORRECT.
2_potential_gain_shortcut.the_shortcut_as_stated_here: references/score-arithmetic.md:113-116 — '**Potential gain** = the dimension points an item recovers × that dimension's weight. Recovering an item is worth 10 dimension points only when the dimension has all ten items scored; with `n` scored items a Fail→Pass flip moves the dimension score by `100/n` and a Partial→Pass flip by `50/n`.' Echoed in the pre-send pass at :149 — 'Every Top 5 gain equals recovered dimension points × weight'.
2_potential_gain_shortcut.arithmetic_check: `100/n × w` is algebraically identical to the corrected sibling form `10 raw points × (10 ÷ n) × w`. The factor that domain-authority-auditor's §5 silently set to 1 is stated explicitly here, in the same sentence, with the all-ten-items case named as the special case rather than the general one. The file also names the case where the shortcut yields zero and says so: :116-118, 'no fix inside A moves the weighted total at all while A is excluded as Insufficient Data — the fix that pays there is supplying the missing site-level data'.
2_potential_gain_shortcut.did_the_deliverables_invent_one: No. Every gain figure in all five deliverables applies the n-dependent form and reproduces exactly on recomputation (worked cases in arithmetic_check.potential_gain_formula). No deliverable printed a flat `points × weight` gain.
2_potential_gain_shortcut.residual_worth_recording: The correct formula is carried at exactly ONE site. `SKILL.md` states no gain arithmetic anywhere, and the Top-5 report template a run copies (SKILL.md:289) reads only '**Impact**: [Fail/Partial] → potential gain of [X] weighted points'. The mirror image of the domain-authority failure: there a wrong formula reached three surfaces, here a right one reaches one. This run opened the reference and got it right — which is evidence the single carrier holds, on one run, at one version. The abbreviated restatement at :149 ('recovered dimension points × weight') would read as the flat form if it were the only line a run saw; it is the F13-r3 shape (a rule stated fully in one paragraph and abbreviated in the checklist a run copies), and it is the line worth hardening if the domain-authority fix is being propagated.
